method.review: Text was extracted from the local official PDF with pypdf and checked around the selected Annex 2b rows. This was not a visual review of the rendered table pages.
method.selectedRows: Nine source-named leads were selected: eight Cavite rivers for the existing pilot and Pagsanjan River as a multi-municipality CALABARZON lead. This is not a transcription of the full regional river inventory.
method.crosswalk: Exact source names and province text were linked to existing leads only for Maragondon River, Pansipit River and Tanay River. Names with suffixes or compound identities were held rather than silently merged.
method.asterisk: The Atlas prints an asterisk after several river names; the reviewed table pages do not explain its meaning. The sourceName field preserves it without interpretation.

terms.sourceNotice: The copyright page permits reproduction in whole or part for educational or non-profit purposes with source acknowledgement.
terms.decision: Attribution is required for the stated permission. The exact intended-use fit and any public derived-database use remain unreviewed; publicationApproval is false. Keep this as a minimal internal factual crosswalk and do not redistribute the PDF, map, or table.

limitations: The 2016 atlas is a historical inventory; it does not establish current river status, a complete CALABARZON river denominator, or fish occurrence.
Source-listed municipalities describe broad locality context, not the exact course, reach, tributaries, estuary, catchability or legal boundaries.
The Atlas cautions that wetland location/boundaries require ground verification and says administrative boundaries are approximate.
No fish presence, fish absence, diet, salinity, fishing access, safety status, geometry, or public app assertion is inferred from this waterbody inventory.
nextAction: Continue source-backed CALABARZON discovery across Batangas, Laguna, Quezon and Rizal; visually review the relevant Atlas pages where needed; obtain independent identity, fish, salinity, geometry and item-specific reuse evidence before any public admission.
